Costa do Sauípe is in the state of Bahia, approximately 70 km from Salvador. Long beaches meet sand dunes, coconut groves, small lakes and tropical vegetation.

Beyond relaxing by the sea, the resort offers a wide range of activities: tennis, golf, horseback riding, cycling and water sports. Hotels also offer fitness and spa programs.

Costa do Sauípe is easy to combine with Salvador on the same trip. The itinerary offers a cultural and urban introduction to Bahia, followed by several quieter days on the coast.

Cousins Rock lies northeast of Santiago, near Bartolomé. Underwater, the dive route alternates between stretches above a reef and sections along a wall. Black corals and small reef inhabitants invite a closer look, while the open water attracts larger animals.

The site description mentions seahorses, barracudas, sea lions, turtles, eagle rays, Galápagos sharks and whitetip reef sharks. Penguins can be seen on the surface. Specific wildlife encounters depend on nature. The program offers a trip to Cousins Rock together with Bartolomé; the journey from the Itabaca Channel takes about 1.5 hours.
